claims.statement: The EBA says financial entities in scope need a comprehensive register of contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers at entity, sub-consolidated, and consolidated levels.
The implementing technical standards for the Register of Information are adopted and published and define templates for contractual arrangements with ICT third-party providers.
The EBA describes the register as part of third-party risk supervision and an input to identifying critical ICT third-party providers.

contrary_evidence: The EBA provides an illustrative spreadsheet, data model, and official materials, so entities with few contracts can maintain the register without another product.
DORA implementation is already underway, meaning many larger buyers have selected tools or consultants.
The presence of template-specific Q&A and changing implementation details increases maintenance cost and error risk.

economics.acquisition_route: Recruit one boutique DORA advisor and 2-3 smaller regulated design partners, demonstrate deterministic validation on redacted contracts, then sell through the advisor channel
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated 5-7 year scenario: 90 entities averaging 60,000 PLN annual revenue yields 5.4m PLN; 35% EBITDA at 4x and 75% ownership implies about 5.67m PLN founder equity value.
economics.founder_time: 16-22 hours per week for a pilot, with financial-regulation interpretation contracted and customer data processed in isolated environments
economics.gross_margin_basis: Taxonomy validation and updates are reusable software; initial contract mapping is service-heavy and must be templated or performed by certified partners
economics.payback: Customer payback hypothesis: reducing annual manual compilation and remediation by 80-200 expert hours could justify a 30,000-90,000 PLN license; baseline labor must be measured
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: 20,000-60,000 PLN setup and 30,000-90,000 PLN annual subscription based on entity, contract, and reporting complexity
economics.retention_or_repeat: Registers must remain updated as contracts, subcontractors, functions, and entities change; source lineage and prior approvals create recurring operational dependence

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A reusable map from real contract language and vendor hierarchies to register fields, validation failures, and remediation patterns without pooling confidential contract text
fingerprint.customer: Smaller Polish/EU insurers, payment institutions, investment firms, credit unions, and regulated groups with many ICT suppliers but limited GRC engineering
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Implementation partnerships with boutique DORA advisors, audit firms, managed security providers, and banking-software consultancies
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Contract ingestion, clause-to-field lineage, vendor/entity resolution, validation, change approvals, and regulator-format export; hypothesis 20,000-60,000 PLN setup plus 30,000-90,000 PLN annually
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: CISO, operational-risk, or compliance leader pays implementation and an annual license per entity or consolidated perimeter
fingerprint.problem_trigger: New or amended ICT contract, acquisition or entity change, annual supervisory request, or failed taxonomy validation

founder_fit: Excellent fit for structured data validation, entity resolution, document AI, and deterministic exports
High contract value allows a small customer count and low-publicity B2B distribution
Can be piloted part-time with redacted or synthetic contracts
Requires strict separation from the founder's employer systems and information
risks: Financial entities may treat contract and operational-resilience data as too sensitive for a small vendor
Established GRC platforms and large consultancies can add the same taxonomy
AI extraction errors must never silently populate a regulatory register
Long procurement and security reviews may conflict with part-time availability

structure.commercial_archetype: Regulatory data compiler licensed per financial entity and reporting perimeter
structure.control_point: The validated DORA Register of Information dataset used for ICT third-party governance and supervisory reporting
structure.critical_dependency: Complete access to vendor contracts, service and entity hierarchies, plus exact implementation of the current ESA data model and reporting taxonomy

thesis: Planning-stage hypothesis: build a contract-to-register compiler for smaller EU financial entities and groups that continuously converts ICT vendor contracts, service inventories, subcontractor chains, and legal-entity relationships into the DORA Register of Information taxonomy. Unlike a generic GRC system, the product would make every source clause and responsible owner traceable to each required field, validate identifiers and primary keys, and generate regulator-ready reporting files. The register becomes a recurring system of record for procurement changes and supervisor submissions, with a narrow Polish implementation-and-validation wedge before expansion through compliance partners.
title: DORA Third-Party Register Compiler
uncertainties: How many small regulated entities still rely on spreadsheets after initial DORA implementation
Procurement willingness to accept a hosted product versus on-premise or private deployment
Frequency and cost of taxonomy updates and supervisory corrections
Whether advisors will channel customers or regard the product as displacing billable work
